raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've been farming my family's land in Quzhou my whole life. My father grew wheat and corn, and I grow wheat and corn. That rotation is what this land knows, and it's what the market here supports. The government still sets a floor price for wheat, which matters to me — I can't afford a bad gamble. I have about 10 mu of flat irrigated land, which I split evenly across the two-season rotation.

My winter wheat is already in the ground from October — right now in April it's heading toward grain fill. I'll keep irrigating and spray once more for aphids and rust before June harvest. After I cut the wheat, I go straight into summer maize. No plowing between — I direct-seed the corn into the stubble to save diesel and time. For wheat I use an improved variety I buy from the county seed station, something like 良星 series; everyone around here uses it. For corn I use hybrid seed, 郑单958 or whatever the seed shop is pushing this year that has a good track record.

I apply urea and diammonium phosphate as base fertilizer for wheat, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate wheat three times — before winter freeze, at jointing, and at heading. Summer gets more rain so the corn usually only needs one irrigation unless July is dry.

I don't experiment. My neighbor tried some new high-yield corn variety two years ago and it lodged badly. I'll stick with what I know.
